page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-8 is configured as a balanced general-purpose virtual machine running on the x86_64 architecture. Compute capacity is delivered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8481C processor, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores via multithreading. Memory allocation is fixed at 32 GB, maintaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory profile of 4 GB per virtual core. Cache hierarchy includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large shared 105 MB L3 cache. Hardware acceleration features Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets for vector and matrix math. The instance provision does not include bundled GPUs, and local disk storage is not attached by default, requiring external network-attached block storage for operating system and application files.

Empirical benchmark results position the instance in the middle tier of general compute servers. Single-core and multi-core evaluations in stress-ng yielded 1621.89 and 6644.93 points respectively, complemented by a Geekbench multi-core rating of 6526.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 11777.79. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 544.66 GB/sec in cached 16 KB read workloads, adjusting to 52.89 GB/sec read and 31.16 GB/sec write on 256 MB uncached buffers. Application throughput tests recorded 8.85 million Redis SET operations per second alongside 12.96 GB/sec for static web serving. Qualitative cost efficiency reflects its standard resource density, offering predictable dedicated performance without paying a premium for accelerators or high-capacity local NVMe drives.

Architectural tradeoffs emerge under specialized data processing tasks. While small language model processing is viable, generating 182.66 tokens per second on a 135M model, heavier tasks such as 7B model generation dropped to 7.39 tokens per second, falling into the bottom quartile alongside multithreaded bzip3 decompression. The absence of local solid-state storage demands reliance on external persistent disks, shifting primary I/O constraints to network-attached storage performance. Consequently, the c3-standard-8 is appropriate for balanced enterprise applications, standard containerized microservices, relational and key-value database nodes with attached storage, API servers, and continuous integration pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. The system provides 32 GB of memory, adhering to a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4 GB per vCPU, and includes 105 MB of L3 cache. It features Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction extensions for accelerated vector and matrix computations. The instance includes no bundled GPUs and has no local ephemeral storage, requiring remote persistent disks for persistent data. Across testing, it exhibits steady average scores across standard compute, memory, and database benchmarks, achieving 8.85 million Redis SET operations per second and 12.96 GB/sec in static web serving. Multithreaded bzip3 decompression and 7B LLM text generation land in lower performance quartiles. This server is best suited for balanced production workloads, including web serving, API gateways, microservices, and enterprise middleware.
